headline: Three-day tobacco permit suspensions approved for 7-Eleven on Mammoth Road and Lowell Quick Stop.
summary: Both cases involved tobacco sales to minors. Under the local rule, the 7-Eleven case counted as a first offense. Reports also covered food inspections, two fires, flu season, and TB follow-up at the clinic.
decisions: Approved a three-day tobacco permit suspension for 7-Eleven, starting November 18th, 5-0 by roll call.
Approved a three-day tobacco permit suspension for Lowell Quick Stop, starting November 18th, with four yes votes recorded.
discussion: 7-Eleven first-offense rule: Members asked whether older violations could bring a stronger penalty. Staff said the local rule copies state language and could be made stricter, but advised against changing it now.
Lowell Quick Stop case: The store sold tobacco before it had a permit, and the owner's letter was read aloud. Concern was raised about sales without a permit.
Restaurant openings: 51 new restaurants opened from January 1st through the day before the report. Six to 10 more were expected before the first of the year.
TB follow-up backlog: Staff said the TB clinic has a backlog of months. The clinic now has two providers each week and doubled appointments.
Measles vaccination: A member asked for MMR vaccination rates in Lowell public schools to be reported at next month's meeting.
